who: Richard B. Latner, historian of the United States at Tulane; PhD Wisconsin 1972.

LC identifies Richard B. Latner as the author of The Presidency of Andrew Jackson (1979).

notes: Institution and doctorate agree; the shared book connects the faculty CV to the authority record.

who: Anne E. (Anne Elisabeth) Lester, medieval historian formerly at Colorado Boulder, subsequently Johns Hopkins; PhD Princeton.

who: Kenneth G. Madison, medieval British historian at Iowa State University.

The 1993 Lake Hendricks diagnostic/feasibility report names Ken Madison of the South Dakota water-resources program; included correspondence calls him a natural resources scientist.

notes: The candidate is the water-resources report author, distinct from Iowa State medieval historian Kenneth G. Madison.

who: Shelby T. (Shelby Thomas) McCloy, historian of France at the University of Kentucky.

LC identifies Shelby T. McCloy with Shelby Thomas McCloy, a historian specializing in France, and cites Gibbon's antagonism to Christianity (1933).

notes: Name, institution during the supervision period, and French historical field agree. The other candidate is Steven G. McCloy, a clinical assistant professor of medicine, according to his LC record.

who: Allen McConnell, historian of Russia at Queens College, CUNY; Columbia PhD dissertation published in 1954.

LC establishes Allen McConnell through Against all idols (1954).
